sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used nationally representative probability samples of students at the fourth and eighth grades in participating countries and benchmarking entities. Countries could elect to assess the fourth grade, the eighth grade, or both; some countries assessed at a higher grade when the target grade was expected to be too difficult (fourth grade assessed at sixth grade in Botswana, Honduras, and Yemen; eighth grade assessed at ninth grade in Botswana, Honduras, and South Africa). The report also applies measurement-quality annotations for countries where achievement is too low for reliable estimation (based on the proportion of students performing below chance), but it does not specify an ML-style analytic inclusion/exclusion rule in the provided excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: TIMSS 2011 International Results in Science reports fourth- and eighth-grade science achievement across 63 countries and 14 benchmarking entities, with optional higher-grade administration when the target grade was too difficult. The science assessment is built from a framework with two dimensions: content domains (life/physical/earth at grade 4; biology/chemistry/physics/earth at grade 8) and cognitive domains (knowing/applying/reasoning at both grades). Achievement is reported on TIMSS scales (0–1000) with a fixed centerpoint of 500 and benchmark thresholds at 400, 475, 550, and 625, describing what students typically know and can do at each level. The report summarizes cross-country differences, trends since 1995, and benchmark attainment (e.g., median shares reaching Low/Intermediate/High/Advanced). It also contextualizes achievement with home resources, school resources and climate, teacher preparation and satisfaction, and student engagement/attitudes, but the excerpted text does not provide an ML predictive modeling framework or PV/missing-data handling details for an empirical ML pipeline.
